report:
PASS applies only to restricted A–H. The current author proof, all four supplements and the complete independent reconstruction establish those statements under the seven specified foundations. This fresh assessment does not replace or alter either retained INCONCLUSIVE report. Original S10 and the unrestricted P01/P17 singularity-class programme remain open.

I checked the mathematical arguments independently; prior verdicts, candidate flags, hashes, compilation receipts, reading declarations and reported symbolic checks were not premises. The seven imported foundations appear below in the required order, each with an exact full quotation from its explicit task grant. All bindings have valid zero-based indices. I also opened the matching primary papers: [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), [BGL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090), [Darvas v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7318v3) and [Berndtsson](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1103.0923). Their relevant contexts agree with the granted scopes. In particular, the bounded BGL construction precedes the global BMP assumption; Darvas concerns a closed Kähler background, uses i∂∂̄ and retains the unnormalized integral norm. Berndtsson’s supplementary construction concerns bounded line-bundle metrics and supports the projective application. The disclosed inherited Bedford–Taylor, closed energy, uniqueness and Calabi–Chen dependencies remain imported foundations; no recursive certification is claimed.

The historical binding map [0,1,1,2,3,4,5,5,6] remains historical evidence. Original passage 2 quotes the BMP assumption in BGL’s different global §2.2. It is preserved as an excluded warning, not positive evidence for foundation 1. The other short historical quotations alone do not substantiate every clause of their indexed statements; the complete contexts and the new full task bindings do. No historical warning is inserted into the new positive-evidence array.

The actual support DAG is acyclic: n1←[]; n2←[n1]; n3←[n1,n2]; n4←[n1,n2,n3]; n5←[n1,n2,n3,n4]; n6←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n7←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n8←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n7]; n9←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n10←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5,n6,n7,n8,n9]. Each mathematical dependency is established below. The explanatory forward reference from n4 to n7 supplies no support for completion and creates no circularity. The supplements supply, respectively, the basic metric construction, full-variation stationarity and diagonal examples, singular examples, and translation saddles; all are incorporated into the current proof and independently reconstructed in the corresponding notes.

A / n2. Write z=e^a w with ||w||=1. The deck transformation increments a by one, proving the smooth identification X≅S^(2n−1)×S¹. The action is free and properly discontinuous; the compact annulus 1≤||z||≤e meets every orbit. Thus the quotient is an actual compact connected complex n-fold. Projective coordinate charts identify π as a holomorphic submersion with fiber C*/e^Z. Scalar multiplication has kernel Z+2πiZ and induces the asserted transitive holomorphic elliptic action. For 1≤k≤n−1, H^(2k)(X,R)=0. A product of two positive-dimensional compact complex manifolds would have a nonzero pullback of a factor’s oriented top class in one of these degrees: fixing a point in the other factor gives a section of its projection. Consequently X admits no such product decomposition.

Put r=log||z||², α=dd^cr=π*κ and β=dr∧d^cr=i∂r∧∂̄r/(2π). Scalar multiplication shifts r by a constant, so the forms descend and are E-invariant. The kernel of α is the vertical complex line, where β is positive; their sum is therefore Hermitian. Direct differentiation gives dβ=−dr∧α, dd^cβ=−α² and dh=−dr∧α≠0. Also β²=0, α^(d+1)=0 and dd^c(h^k)=−kα^(k+1). On a fiber, with scalar coordinate a+ib, r=2a+constant and d^cr=db/(2π). Thus β=da∧db/π; its periods 1 and 2π give fiber integral 2. Hence h^n=nβ∧α^d and ∫Xh^n=2n. The background is big in the original sense with ρ=0 and ε=1.

For reverse current positivity, work in a holomorphic submersion chart with vertical coordinate w. Its coefficient r_w is nonzero. Every smooth base-and-strip (1,0) vector ξ has the lift ξ−∂r(ξ)∂w/r_w, which annihilates ∂r. Contracting π*T+β with this lift removes β exactly, where T=pr_Y*κ+dd^cV. Testing the resulting distribution against nonnegative compact fiber densities transfers positivity to T. Conversely positive T pulls back positively and β can be added. This argument tests currents on open charts; it never restricts a singular current to a fiber. An invariant locally integrable potential descends as a distribution. Canonical recovery, or local holomorphic sections, produces its genuine base representative; equality of canonical representatives holds everywhere, including poles. The same reasoning works on strips, and strict spatial positivity in the smooth case is equivalent to strict base positivity.

B / n3. For bounded v, locally add a smooth base potential for κ and approximate the resulting bounded psh function decreasingly by smooth psh functions. Foundation 0 identifies their closed products, while foundation 1 supplies the nonclosed smooth-correction polynomial. In the expansion of (π*(κ+dd^cv)+β)^n, horizontal degree n=d+1 and β² both vanish. Therefore the actual bounded product is nβ∧π*(κ+dd^cv)^d.

For arbitrary canonical v, use v_j=max(v,−j). Exactly, π*v_j=max(π*v,−j), including pole values. Multiplication by the genuine strict-superlevel indicator gives
1_{π*v>−j}(h+dd^cπ*v_j)^n=nβ∧π*[1_{v>−j}(κ+dd^cv_j)^d].
The base measures increase by locality and have mass at most one, since each bounded closed-base product has total mass one. Hence the Hopf measures increase with mass at most 2n. Their limit is precisely the canonical non-pluripolar construction and equals nβ∧π*MAκ(v). Concretely, β∧π*μ is the measure defined by integrating a Borel function over each fiber against β and then against μ. No arbitrary rough-current pullback is needed. Every finite-level measure vanishes on every pluripolar set by foundation 1; its increasing setwise limit does likewise. Thus there is no pole-set product and no Hopf BMP invocation. Tonelli and the fiber integral 2 give the stated integration identity for every nonnegative Borel F, including infinite integrals.

For the full Perron problem, local spatial domination by a smooth psh potential makes restriction of each competitor to a temporal complex line subharmonic or identically −∞. Imaginary invariance yields temporal convexity, hence W_t≤(1−t)π*v_0+tπ*v_1. This bounds the whole family locally above. Its canonical upper envelope retains h-positivity: locally approximate h from above by closed constant forms within an arbitrary positive error, apply psh upper-envelope stability after adding their potentials, and let the error tend to zero. A base competitor supplies nontriviality.

The entire full-X competitor family is permuted by E, so its supremum and usc regularization are invariant. A makes its descent a base subgeodesic. The chord bound survives regularization and preserves the original joint boundary upper bounds. At a pole, the relevant endpoint is below every prescribed negative constant in a neighborhood, while the other endpoint has a finite upper bound; this proves the joint bound there too. Thus the descended envelope is a base competitor. Conversely every base competitor pulls back. These two inclusions prove equality of the full envelopes. Open submersion charts ensure commutation with usc regularization. The same chord argument reconciles the printed pointwise temporal boundary convention with the required joint convention.

For E² endpoints, foundation 3 gives a nontrivial E² rooftop, which is a constant-in-time competitor, and gives genuine base endpoint convergence. The identity ∫X|π*(v_t−v_i)|h^n/(2n)=∫Y|v_t−v_i|κ^d transfers L¹ convergence. Every prescribed smooth positive probability dV has bounded positive density ratio with h^n/(2n) on compact X, so convergence also holds in the original L¹(X,dV). The canonical endpoints and their poles are unchanged. No Hopf capacity comparison is used.

C / n4. Smooth basic positive potentials and smooth basic paths correspond bijectively to smooth positive base potentials and paths. B gives G_X(π*ξ,π*η)=2n∫Yξη(κ+dd^cv)^d. For f=v/(2π), κ+i∂∂̄f=κ+dd^cv, while tangent vectors acquire the factor 2π. Thus taking precisely the basic smooth path infima gives d_B=2π√(2n)d_D on the scaled base potentials. Foundation 2 applies because Y=P^d is connected, compact and Kähler. It identifies the completion with canonical full-mass finite-second-moment potentials; B converts these conditions exactly to actual Hopf mass 2n and finite squared Hopf moment. Constant metric rescaling preserves completeness, CAT(0) geometry and unique constant-speed segments. B identifies those segments with the full Hermitian Perron envelopes.

For smooth v, v+tc is its base Perron segment, and foundation 6 gives base distance |c| since the base mass is one. Constant addition is an isometry on the smooth path metric and extends to its completion. Approximation therefore gives d_B(u,u+c)=√(2n)|c| also at singular completion points, without a singular initial-velocity formula. No nonbasic path enters this definition.

D / n5. For an absolutely continuous metric curve, endpoint distance is at most length. Cauchy–Schwarz gives A_B≥d_B(p,q)²/2. Equality forces constant speed and length equal to distance; subinterval length bounds combined with the endpoint triangle inequality then force the metric-segment identity on every subinterval. Unique geodesics give the unique minimizer. For coincident endpoints, equality forces the constant curve.

The smooth-speed assertion needs an argument. Set Δ=v_{s+δ}−v_s. C¹ dependence in spatial C² gives ||Δ||C²=O(|δ|), Δ/δ→dot v_s and time remainder o(δ). On the auxiliary unit interval, the chord has uniformly positive spatial form and mixed coefficients O(|δ|). Subtracting Kδ²τ(1−τ), with sufficiently large uniform K, makes the temporal coefficient dominate the squared mixed Schur complement, producing a subgeodesic with the exact endpoints. Its Perron segment G satisfies chord−Kδ²τ(1−τ)≤G≤chord, so Δ−Kδ²≤dot G_0≤Δ. Foundation 6 applies only to these smooth positive endpoints. After the operator conversion, division of its distance identity by δ² proves the raw base norm as metric speed. Multiplication by 2n proves the raw Hopf norm. Smooth path-length bounds ensure absolute continuity, so integrating gives A_B=S_X. The completed action remains defined by metric speed.

For full-variation stationarity, differentiate the original action at a smooth positive basic Perron path:
L(w)=∫₀¹∫X[dot u dot w ω_u^n+(n/2)dot u²dd^cw∧ω_u^(n−1)]dt.
This is the full differential, including the terms that generate torsion upon spatial integration by parts. The action is E-invariant and u is E-fixed, hence L(w)=L(∫E g*w dg). The average is a smooth basic variation with zero endpoints. Uniform positivity makes every smooth direction admissible for sufficiently small parameter. Before differentiating, the basic action is exactly 2n times the closed-base action. With η=κ+dd^cv and f=dot v, closed spatial Stokes and time integration by parts give
L_Y(q)=∫q[−ddot v η^d+d df∧d^cf∧η^(d−1)]dt.
The identity dd^c(f²)=2fdd^cf+2df∧d^cf cancels the mixed terms. Foundation 5 applies to the smooth bounded base endpoints. The smooth homogeneous equation has spatial block (i/(2π))G and mixed entries ∂f/2; its Schur complement gives ddot v=G^{j bar k}f_j f_bar k, equivalently ddot v η^d=d df∧d^cf∧η^(d−1). Therefore L_Y and every full-X L vanish. No torsion term was deleted, and no primitive was introduced on X. Directly, dd^cω_u^(n−1)=−(n−1)α²∧π*η^(n−2)=0 by base degree. This is stationarity, not full-X minimization.

E / n6. The projective ratio is a genuine global smooth potential. The holomorphic strip map F([z],s)=[e^(a_js/2)z_j] gives pr_Y*κ+dd^cV=F*κ. It has rank d, zero (d+1)st power and strictly positive spatial slices. Foundation 5 identifies this bounded solution with the base Perron segment. B and D give the full Hopf segment and all-variation stationarity.

Changing variables by F_t makes the squared base velocity independent of t. Under mass-one Fubini–Study, x_j=|z_j|²/Σ|z_l|² have uniform simplex distribution, with moments E[x_i²]=2/[n(n+1)] and E[x_ix_j]=1/[n(n+1)] for i≠j. Thus the squared base speed is [(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/[n(n+1)]. Multiplying by 2n yields the asserted squared distance, and the action is half that value. For n=3 and (1,−1,0), these are 1 and 1/2. At coordinate points, v_t=ta_j; unequal a_j prove spatial nonconstancy for t>0.

F / n7. For each finite C, the full obstacle family below 0 and π*v+C is nonempty: π*v+K works for K≤C and K≤−sup v. It is bounded above and E-invariant. Its envelope remains below the usc obstacles, descends by A, and contains the pullbacks of all base obstacle competitors. Therefore the finite-C envelopes commute with pullback. Taking their increasing union and canonical usc representative gives P_h[π*v]=π*Pκ[v]. This proves the model embedding without treating the final projection as an ordinary-equivalent competitor.

For a full-mass base potential, scale it by 1/(2π) and apply foundation 4 with full-mass obstacle zero. Scaling the potentials and order constants converts the resulting source envelope back to the original convention. Its value is zero. Consequently every B₂ point projects to model zero, although d_B distinguishes points and constants. It cannot descend through that projection or ordinary equivalence. For ordinary-equivalent endpoints, affine maximum barriers and the chord bound give their common ordinary type at every interior slice, including common poles. None of these calculations computes lower or upper mass over the full Hopf ordinary type, whose representatives need not be basic.

Pointwise suprema and infima commute with pullback, and open submersions commute with usc regularization. Both Legendre operations therefore commute, preserving model normalization, concavity, monotonicity and pole values. Under the explicit antecedent that the associated base Perron ray has every finite slice in E², each finite restriction is a base Perron segment and B–D apply. Its pulled-back restriction is a d_B geodesic and unique metric-action minimizer. On an interval of duration T−s the minimum is d_B(u_s,u_T)²/[2(T−s)], or d_B²/2 after unit-interval rescaling. The finite-energy antecedent is retained; no unconditional stretching-envelope or topology conclusion follows.

G / n8. In the affine chart put s=log|w|², L=log(1+e^s), p=e^s/(1+e^s), q=1+L−s and H=L+1−q^a. Its slope P=p+a(1−p)q^(a−1) is positive, and
P_s=p(1−p)(1−a q^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−p)²q^(a−2)>0.
The radial Levi eigenvalues are P/|w|² with multiplicity d−1 and P_s/|w|² in the radial direction. This proves positivity off o. The homogeneous formula is smooth across infinity, where v_a=0. Canonical cutoffs have local psh potentials max(H,L−j), equal to L−j near o. They decrease to a nontrivial genuine κ-psh representative with value −∞ at o. Polynomial growth in |s| against exponential radial volume verifies local integrability. Its supremum is zero.

The exact determinant is (dd^cH)^d=(d!/π^d)P^(d−1)P_s|w|^(−2d)dλ. The sphere area 2π^d/(d−1)! and ds=2dR/R give radial measure dP^(d−1)P_s ds times normalized angular measure. Hence the annular flux is exactly P^d, with no omitted dimensional or π factor. Equivalently, d^cs has circle integral one and dd^cs induces mass-one Fubini–Study on P^(d−1).

In q coordinates, p=e^(1−q) and −P_q=p(1−a q^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−p)q^(a−2). The slope decreases from one to zero. At canonical level j the strict superlevel is q<Q_j=(1+j)^(1/a). Locality excludes the inner constant region and any cutoff-shell measure; its actual finite-level mass is exactly 1−P(Q_j)^d. The smooth hyperplane at infinity has zero measure. Increasing canonical levels therefore give actual full mass one and no pole atom.

The exact second moment is the integral from 1 to infinity of
(q^a−1)² dP(q)^(d−1)[p(1−a q^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−p)q^(a−2)]dq.
Its tail is asymptotic to d a^d(1−a)q^((d+2)a−d−1), with positive leading constant. Thus finiteness is equivalent to a<d/(d+2). At equality, truncation at Q gives d a^d(1−a)log Q+O(1): residual power corrections are integrable and exponential corrections negligible. B gives exactly the Hopf multiplier 2n for mass and moment. The genuine pole is the whole elliptic fiber over o. For a<b, v_b≤v_a but v_a−v_b=q^b−q^a→∞, so mutual ordinary order fails. In the subcritical range, C gives finite positive distance and F gives both zero model projections.

H / n9. The radius r is globally defined modulo two, so all displayed periodic functions descend smoothly. Spatial differentiation gives h+dd^cu=(1+u_r)α+(1+u_rr)β. Strict positivity is equivalent to positivity of both coefficients. Fiber integration gives the exact raw action n∫₀¹〈u_t²(1+u_r)^d(1+u_rr)〉dt, with 〈F〉=(1/2)∫₀²Fdr. Temporal convexity bounds every full strip competitor from 0 to c by ct, which is itself a competitor. Thus ct is the full Perron segment.

Its first variation is c∫w_t h^n+(nc²/2)∫dd^cw∧h^d. Fixed endpoints eliminate the time term, and dd^c(h^d)=0 with smooth Stokes eliminates the spatial term for every full-X variation. The full Hessian is
∫[w_t²h^n+2ncw_tdd^cw∧h^d+(ndc²/2)(dd^cw)²∧h^(d−1)]dt.
For radial endpoint-zero directions, periodic integration removes w_rw_rr, while ∫〈w_tw_rr〉dt=−[〈w_r²〉]₀¹/2=0. It reduces exactly to
Q(w)=2n∫〈(w_t+dcw_r)²−d(d+1)c²w_r²/2〉dt.
For w_k=sin(πt)cos(πk(r−dct)), Q(w_k)=nπ²[1−d(d+1)c²k²/2]/2. Distinct positive integer modes are orthogonal under radial averaging. The algebraic span of sufficiently large modes is therefore an infinite-dimensional negative subspace. Each fixed finite combination has bounded derivatives and admits arbitrarily small strictly positive spatial variations. A negative direction lowers action near the stationary path, proving failure of local raw-action minimality in the smooth full-X path class.

For the explicit threefold path, positivity follows from 1−π|ε| and 1−π²|ε|. To verify the action, set f=sin(πt), p=f′ and θ=π(r−2t). Then w_t=p cosθ+2πf sinθ, w_r=−πf sinθ and w_rr=−π²f cosθ. Expand (1+εw_t)²(1+εw_r)²(1+εw_rr). Its averaged quadratic coefficient is p²/2−3π²f²/2−π²fp; its quartic coefficient is π²f²p²/8+3π⁴f³p/4+3π⁴f⁴/2. Odd powers vanish by the angular half-turn, and the polynomial has degree five, so there are no further even terms. The time integrals are −π²/2 and 37π⁴/64. Multiplication by three proves exactly 3−3π²ε²/2+111π⁴ε⁴/64. At ε=1/100 it is 2.998521248778759<3; positivity holds, and the strict inequality follows exactly from ε²<32/(37π²).

For every c≠0, a sufficiently small negative-direction variation has action below nc². Cauchy–Schwarz gives L_raw²≤2S_X<2nc², proving the strict comparison with √(2n)|c|. These are legitimate full-path competitors and need not be strip subgeodesics. No definiteness or completion of the full length infimum is inferred.

Corrections and historical comparison. The four disclosed source changes correctly delimit bounded BGL use, supply the arbitrary-dV endpoint passage, add the cohomological nonproduct proof and attribute plurifine locality to Bedford–Taylor 1987. The old b₁ comparison alone excluded Y×E; the stronger current assertion requires—and now has—the additional cohomological argument. This is an added proof, not merely a wording change. The older private short-segment argument is valid under its O(δ²) time-remainder antecedent, but C¹ alone does not establish that antecedent. Current43ebad and n5 supply the correct o(δ) argument while retaining the independent O(δ²) Schur barrier. The target smooth-speed conclusion is therefore established by the current proof. Frozen n1 remains unchanged, but its extra mean-zero Green normalization assertion is excluded as source evidence. Printed Darvas §7 does not impose it; a unit-Dirac coefficient presupposes volume one, with Vδ_o at volume V. A–H never use that illustrative coefficient. The directly verified singular-velocity warning remains intact. These historical issues leave no unresolved defect in the operative A–H proof.

The restricted construction is substantive scoped progress: it provides a complete metric and coherent metric-speed action on genuine basic potentials of a nonclosed, nonproduct manifold, identifies the full Perron interpolation, proves full-variation smooth stationarity, and includes spatially nonconstant and genuinely singular examples. Its complete topology is a potential topology with constants retained. Model projection collapses the whole completed domain to zero, and positive constant distances prevent descent to ordinary types. It establishes no full-type volume formula, Hopf BMP theorem, unrestricted nonbasic completion, ideal-model metric or separating singularity-class topology. Completion of original S10/P01/P17 requires a further construction or argument.

passages.statement: For 1≤p≤m and locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a domain in C^m, their mixed Bedford–Taylor product is a positive closed current, symmetric and multilinear, and is continuous under pointwise decreasing sequences whose limits remain locally bounded. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

passages.statement: For smooth real (1,1)-forms θ_i, not necessarily closed, and bounded quasi-psh φ_i, the product of T_i=θ_i+dd^cφ_i is the symmetric multilinear smooth-correction polynomial in local closed dd^c products. For potentials bounded on a compact K, the restricted product depends only on T_i, is non-pluripolar, is plurifinely local, is compatible with restriction, and is positive when all T_i are positive. These bounded local statements require no BMP hypothesis. BGL 2406.01090, §2.1, equations 2.1–2.5 and Proposition 2.1.

On a connected compact Kähler manifold with operator i∂∂̄, if f_0 has full non-pluripolar mass and f_1 is a canonical plurisubharmonic potential, then P[f_1](f_0)=f_0 if and only if f_1 has full mass, where P[f_1](f_0)=usc lim_{C→∞}P(min(f_1+C,f_0)). Darvas 1401.7318v3, Theorem 4.3.

For bounded canonical endpoints on a connected compact Kähler manifold, the bounded imaginary-invariant homogeneous Monge–Ampère Dirichlet solution on the strip is unique and equals the subgeodesic Perron envelope with endpoint upper bounds. Darvas 1401.7318v3, §2.2, equations 16–17; the projective bounded-envelope construction and uniform endpoint limits also appear in Berndtsson 1103.0923, §2.2.

For smooth strictly positive endpoints f_0,f_1 on a connected compact Kähler manifold, their weak segment g satisfies d(f_0,f_1)²=∫_Y(dot g_0)²(κ+i∂∂̄f_0)^m for the unnormalized Mabuchi path metric, with the one-sided initial velocity. Darvas 1401.7318v3, equation 15.
